paper_metadata.title: Thermal stability, microstructure and texture evolution of thermomechanical processed AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic high entropy alloy

evidence.quote: The microstructural and texture evoluti ons of as-cast AlCoCrFeNi 2.1 eutectic high entropy alloy (EHEA) have been investigated in the course of thermomechanical processing at the temperature range of 25-500°C.
The room and high temperature deformation behavior of AlCoCrFeNi2.1 EHEA was assessed through conducting tensile tests at 25 °C up to 500 °C.
The experimented material was received in vacuum arc remelted condition by the nominal composition Al-Co-Cr-Fe-2.1Ni (in aspect ra tio of at. %).

The specimens for high-temperature deformation were initially pre-hea ted to the specified temperature and soaked isothermally for 10 min.
Tensile tests at room and elevated temperatures (25 °C, 300 °C, and 500 °C) were carried out using a GOTECH AI-7000 universal testing machine coupled with a programmable resistance furnace.
Tensile tests were then performed under the strain rate of 0.001s -1 up to fracture.
After the fracture, the specimens w ere immediately quenched in water to preserve the deformed microstructures.

attributes.morphology: stretched and broken with slight deviation from load direction

evidence.quote: By increasing temperature up to 300 ℃, similar to room temperature, stretched and broken dendrites wi th a slight deviation in the direction of the load are formed.
a greater number of broken dendrites along with a higher fraction of LAGBs can be detected compared to that of room temperature condition.

Mentioned features a re mainly attributed to enhancement in dislocation cross ability and formation of sub-grai n boundaries at 300 ℃ temperature in comparison to room temperature ( Fig. 5b ), which is in good agreement with other reports [16].
